content.text: The visible test passes. The two failures are bugs in my own check expectations, not the implementation: (1) one "schema-invalid" line was actually valid after my `.replace()` made it a valid record with an extra field; (2) I asserted `durationMs === 12` while including a 999 ms failed job (sum is 1011). Rerunning with corrected expectations:

That failure is a PowerShell host quirk with capturing native stdout (`StandardOutputEncoding...`), not a sandbox denial. Let me probe which output-handling construct works in this host before rerunning the CLI checks.

Now it's clear: PowerShell only breaks when a native command's output would be *captured* (assignment/function), which forces the broken decode path. Top-level standalone `cmd /c "..."` calls with the redirection inside cmd work (Probe C). Restructuring without any helper function or assignment around the cmd calls:

c1 passed fully via fd redirection; c2's output is unexpectedly missing. I need diagnostics instead of a crash — making the battery resilient and reporting each case's status/error/stderr even when the output is absent:

All checks complete. Final report:

## Changed files (exactly the three allowed)
- `parse.mjs` — `parseJobs(text)`: `TypeError` on non-string; strips leading BOM; LF/CRLF + blank-line handling with physical 1-based line numbers; non-null non-array objects only; `id` 1–32 ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; integer, nonnegative, finite `durationMs` (incl. `1e400` → `SCHEMA`, `-0` normalized to `+0`); status whitelist; extra fields dropped; error precedence `INVALID_JSON` → `SCHEMA` → `DUPLICATE_ID` with string codes and no raw input; invalid records never reserve ids; first valid per id kept.
- `aggregate.mjs` — `summarizeJobs(jobs)`: counts all, sums only succeeded/failed, success-only median (even count via `a/2 + b/2`, overflow-free), slowest top-3 non-skipped sorted by duration desc then ASCII id asc, returns copies, never mutates input; zeroed empty summary.
- `cli.mjs` — exactly two args; equal resolved paths rejected before any file change; reads input fully before touching output; recursive parent creation; exclusive `wx` uniquely named sibling temp, write, close, atomic rename; cleanup only of owned temp files; preserves existing output on any failure; exit 0 (clean), 2 (errors published), 1 (arg/read/write failure) with concise sanitized stderr and no stdout output; no services/background work.

## Actual test result
`node visible-test.mjs` → **`3 visible assertions passed`** (exit 0), run twice. Fixture dir contains only the three source files plus `visible-test.mjs` (byte count 511, untouched).

Additional self-testing (no extra files in the fixture; scratch only under the platform temp area, removed afterward):
- ~30 inline module checks on parser/aggregator edge cases — all passed (two initial failures were expectation bugs in my own checks, corrected and re-passed).
- 33 CLI end-to-end checks — all passed: exit codes 0/1/2, nested output dir creation, atomic replacement, existing-output preservation on input-read failure, equal-path rejection, wrong arg counts + usage, silent stdout on every path, sanitized stderr, no leftover temp files, BOM/CRLF/blank-line reports, JSON layout with trailing newline.

## Blocked checks / environment notes
- **Pipe-based child-output capture is blocked by the sandbox (EPERM)** — attempted once per the contract, not retried. stdout/stderr silence was instead verified via OS-level fd redirection to files (no pipes), so that guarantee is still checked. Codex should re-run the integration tests in an unrestricted environment.
- The pwsh host here also cannot capture/redirect native-command output at all (`StandardOutputEncoding is only supported when standard output is redirected`); this was worked around with the fd/`cmd`-free harness above and does not affect the implementation.

## Unresolved issues
None in the implementation against the stated requirements; `visible-test.mjs` and all constraints (3 files, Node 24 built-ins only, no network/packages/delegation) hold.
